subject: CFA with WSMLV -- How to Interpret Output?

messages.author: 46d933c71b5b2f22
messages.subject: CFA with WSMLV -- How to Interpret Output?
parts:
Hello,

I am relatively new to CFAs and need help determining what values to actually use when evaluating my model's fit. 

I am doing a factor analysis on the AMAS scale. This scale has 9 items, 2 subscales, and is scored 1 to 5. Here is my code.

model1 <- '
  learning =~ AMAS1 + AMAS3 + AMAS6 + AMAS7 + AMAS9
  testing  =~ AMAS5 + AMAS2 + AMAS4 + AMAS8
'
fit1 <- cfa(model1, data = MFsex_clean, ordered = c("AMAS1", "AMAS2", "AMAS3", "AMAS4", "AMAS5", "AMAS6", "AMAS7", "AMAS8", "AMAS9"), meanstructure=TRUE, missing = "listwise", estimator = "WLSMV")
summary(fit1,fit.measures=TRUE, standardized = TRUE)

I am confused about how to assess the fit of this model. For example, I do not know whether to use the scaled CFI or the robust scaled CFI. Here are some values if it is helpful:
standard CFI: 0.997
scaled CFI: 0.989
robust CFI: 0.961

Which value is the valid one to use?

Side question: I also want to do measurement invariance and compare the fit of some models. What values should I use for comparing the fits of CFAs using ordinal data?

messages.author: 8c5a85ec8479672a
messages.subject: Re: CFA with WSMLV -- How to Interpret Output?
parts:
Hello, 

Someone may have a better answer and an actual guidance on which value to choose. However, I would like to share three articles that show why something that seems to invoke a very basic answer, may not be so simple. Hopefully it helps somehow: 

(i) see for a clarification on the differences between those, but most importantly see also the section "A note of caution": https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/epdf/10.1080/00273171.2018.1455142?needAccess=true. 

(ii) see the simulations in here and results because they address the specific estimator in question: https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-018-1055-2. 

(iii) sometimes I wonder if the differences (in your case) are even that relevant, but this is like a can of worms to be honest: https://link.springer.com/article/10.3758/s13428-023-02193-3

Best,
Felipe.
